code_safety.reason: 1 finding from checks whose precision is not yet measured is listed but not deducted

evidence.label: mcp-js-ssrf-nonliteral-url (medium/low)
evidence.detail: An outbound request is made to a URL that is not a literal. If any part is caller-supplied the server can be aimed at internal hosts it can reach and the caller cannot.

evidence.label: mcp-js-ssrf-metadata-endpoint (medium/low)
evidence.detail: Listed, not deducted: this check is new and its precision has not been measured, so it is shown for review and scores nothing. A string literal names the cloud instance-metadata endpoint, which serves a hosted instance's credentials to anything on it that asks. Code that contacts it can be the last step of an SSRF; the same literal is also how an SSRF defence names what it blocks, and a pattern cannot tell the two apart, so this is listed for review and not deducted.

evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: no authentication appears in the source we fetched, but this server's network endpoint is a hosted remote, whose authentication can be enforced in front of its code — and no credential header is declared. An undeclared header is not an absent one, so `03` §4's "no authentication" band is not established.

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared endpoint(s) are HTTPS: https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/calendar; scored 80, not 100: `03` §4 reserves 100 for HTTPS *with HSTS*, and an HSTS header can only be seen by connecting, which `04` §9 does not do. This is an unverifiable band, not an observed absence.

evidence.label: secret_handling
evidence.detail: detect-secrets matched 6 credential-shaped string(s), every one from a keyword or entropy heuristic (Hex High Entropy String). Those flag placeholders, variable names and content hashes as readily as credentials, so they do not establish the committed credential `03` §4's 0 asserts, and this sub-check is not scored; Hex High Entropy String at server.appointment.json:28; Hex High Entropy String at server.itinerary.json:28; Hex High Entropy String at server.json:29; Hex High Entropy String at server.json.pub:28; Hex High Entropy String at server.mcpb.json:29; Hex High Entropy String at server.variant.json:28

evidence.label: authorization_granularity
evidence.detail: 10 tool registrations and no conditional access logic found — `03` §4 calls this case 'needs human review' and assigns it no score band, so it is not scored here

evidence.label: issue_responsiveness
evidence.detail: every issue read was filed by the project itself (3 by its maintainers or bots), so none is someone outside waiting for an answer, and `03` §5's question — will anyone read an issue I file? — has nothing to measure.

evidence.label: release_cadence
evidence.detail: released 29 day(s) ago (by releases), inside `03` §5's 30-day window

evidence.label: bus_factor
evidence.detail: this repository's 12-month history is longer than the bounded walk `04` §7 performs, and the authors found so far span more than one of `03` §5's bands. A limit of ours, not a finding about the server.

evidence.label: repository_signals
evidence.detail: `03` §5 scores this by quartile WITHIN the server's category, which needs a distribution across every scanned server and so cannot be computed while scanning one. It is a post-pass over the crawl and that pass does not exist yet.

dependency_health.reason: no lockfile in the fetched source; dependency versions are unresolved, so no vulnerability can be attributed

evidence.label: license
evidence.detail: LICENSE present with no SPDX-License-Identifier tag; identified as 'MIT' from its text

evidence.label: readme_quality
evidence.detail: README.md: installation instructions (+25), configuration documented (+25), exposed tools or resources enumerated (+30)

evidence.label: declared_scopes
evidence.detail: neither the README nor the MCP manifest documents what the server accesses or what side effects it has

evidence.label: changelog
evidence.detail: no CHANGELOG in the fetched source. `03` §7's partial credit for tagged releases carrying release notes is not applied here — that needs the forge API, which this check does not call

evidence.label: security_contact
evidence.detail: no SECURITY.md and no disclosure contact in the README, so a finder has no route to report a vulnerability privately
